class.name: ShaderSky
class.brief_description: A [Sky] whose contents come from a custom [code]shader_type sky;[/code] shader.
class.description: Assign a [ShaderMaterial] whose shader begins with [code]shader_type sky;[/code] to [member sky_material] and drop this resource on a [WorldEnvironment]'s sky slot ([member Environment.background_sky], with [member Environment.background_mode] set to [b]Sky[/b] or [b]Color+Sky[/b]). The visible sky is drawn by running the shader once per screen pixel (sharp, full resolution, no projection distortion). Separately, a small equirectangular panorama is baked from the shader and fed through the regular radiance pipeline so the sky also lights the scene and appears in reflections, like a [PanoramaSky]. That radiance bake is [b]coalesced to at most ~2 Hz[/b] no matter how often the material or its parameters change (rebuilding it is expensive), so a per-frame day/night script won't stall the frame rate. Ambient light updates a little behind the visible sky as a result. All [code]uniform[/code] parameters declared by the shader are editable on the [ShaderMaterial] (in the inspector and at runtime via [method ShaderMaterial.set_shader_param]). [b]Note:[/b] Shader skies require the GLES3 renderer. Under GLES2 the sky is left unchanged. The sky [code]fragment()[/code] function receives [code]EYEDIR[/code] (world-space view direction), [code]SKY_COORDS[/code] (equirect UV, [code].y[/code] 0 = up, 1 = down), [code]POSITION[/code] (camera position), [code]TIME[/code], [code]AT_CUBEMAP_PASS[/code] (true only during the radiance bake), and [code]LIGHT0..3_ENABLED/DIRECTION/COLOR/ENERGY[/code] for the scene's [DirectionalLight]s. Write [code]COLOR[/code] (and optionally [code]ALPHA[/code]).

members.member: Width in pixels of the internal panorama baked for radiance/ambient only (height is half). This does [i]not[/i] affect the visible sky, which is drawn per screen pixel — keep it small (256 is plenty for lighting).
When the radiance/ambient bake is refreshed. The visible sky always animates every frame regardless. See [enum ProcessMode].
The [ShaderMaterial] providing the sky. Its shader must start with [code]shader_type sky;[/code].

constants.constant: Refresh the radiance bake only when [member sky_material] or one of its parameters changes. Best when the sky animates visually but its lighting is roughly constant (day scene, slow clouds).
Also refresh the radiance bake a few times per second, so ambient light and reflections follow the animation (sunset, aurora, fast weather).
